overview: In-depth knowledge of modules 3 and 4 plus practical skills from modules 1 and 2 is needed; candidates had enough time and achieved a good spread of marks.
State the equation, substitute data and then evaluate in every numerical answer; many weaker answers omitted clear substitution.
Definitions and technical terms were often imprecise; explanation answers lacked detail.
In planning questions identify independent, dependent and control variables and how each is measured.
In 'show' questions make the method explicit and finish by comparing the result to the given value; using the 'show' value earns nothing.
Several optical and de Broglie questions were omitted by a significant number of candidates.
assessment_for_learning: Practise drawing tangents that span as much of the graph as possible.
For gradients choose two easily read points on the line, far apart, substitute into (y2-y1)/(x2-x1); y-intercept = y - mx using one of those points.
Practise expressing units in SI base units and checking homogeneity of equations.
Know how light gates with a timer measure velocity and acceleration, including interrupt-card length; also know motion sensors.
Choose graph axes to linearise a relationship and explain how constants come from gradient and intercept.
Treat horizontal and vertical components of projectile motion independently.
At the critical angle the refraction angle is 90 degrees, so sin 90 = 1.
With powers of ten, write the equation, substitute with powers included and write intermediate values down.
